headline: Madrasa teacher jailed in Tangail for alleged sexual assault of 10-year-old student
summary: Police arrested the teacher, Al Amin, after the victim's mother filed a case. Authorities plan to file a remand prayer for further questioning.
details: A madrasa teacher was sent to jail on Friday by a Tangail court for allegedly sexually assaulting his 10-year-old male student in Mirzapur upazila.

caption:
A 10-year-old male student was allegedly sexually assaulted by his madrasa teacher in Tangail. The teacher has been sent to jail.

A madrasa teacher was sent to jail on Friday by a Tangail court for allegedly sexually assaulting his 10-year-old male student in Mirzapur upazila.

Police arrested the teacher, identified as Al Amin, after the victim's mother filed a case against him with Mirzapur Police Station around noon.

The accused was subsequently sent to jail through a Tangail court in the afternoon. Police officials have stated their intention to file a remand prayer to question him further.

According to the case statement, the boy had been enrolled at the madrasa in January. He later fell ill and contacted his mother, requesting to be taken home.

The boy was then taken to Kumudini Hospital for treatment, where a doctor informed the family that he had allegedly been sexually assaulted. The boy later disclosed to his family that Al Amin had allegedly been raping him for the past three months.

headline_marked: [[Yemen's Houthis seize Bab al-Mandab Strait]] and Red Sea islands, impacting global trade
headline: Yemen's Houthis seize Bab al-Mandab Strait and Red Sea islands, impacting global trade
summary: The lightning offensive gives Houthis control over a crucial shipping corridor, potentially deepening the Middle East war's impact on international commerce and Saudi oil exports.
details: The Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast and captured three strategic islands yesterday. This lightning offensive cemented their hold on a vital shipping corridor linking Europe and Asia.

After a week-long offensive that left hundreds dead, government officials confirmed the Houthis now control the Yemeni side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This includes Mayyun, Greater Hanish, and Lesser Hanish islands, completing their takeover of the western coast.

The capture of these islands, particularly Mayyun in the middle of the strait, significantly heightens the Houthis’ ability to attack Saudi tankers. Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest oil exporter, has relied on the Red Sea since Iran’s Hormuz blockade choked off its shipments via the Gulf.

An adviser to Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei congratulated the Houthis on their “resounding victory,” stating Iran now controls two strategic chokepoints. This development has contributed to oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel this week.

The Houthis' military spokesman declared navigation through the Bab al-Mandab Strait “safe” for all but Saudi ships, which have been banned. The offensive has cost over 500 lives and displaced approximately 46,000 people, according to the UN migration agency.

This week, the Houthis also carried out their heaviest missile and drone attack in years against Saudi Arabia, setting oil sites ablaze and wounding 73. Separately, a US official reported Iranian strikes damaged multiple American military aircraft in Jordan.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly urged US President Donald Trump to launch strikes against the Houthis, but Trump rejected the request. US officials stated the administration does not intend to take direct military action against the Houthis at this time.
